- [**ScooterLink: reconstructing Honda RoadSync’s handlebar-button protocol**](https://github.com/gdorgian/ScooterLink) - Replaces Honda RoadSync’s Apple Music-only media control with an iOS app that pairs with a Honda PCX 2025 TFT dash over Bluetooth Low Energy and turns handlebar presses into system-wide commands for any player. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · Also: Protocol · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/scooterlink-honda-roadsync-case/)</sub>

- [**trvision: implementing Thermalright Vision USB display control**](https://github.com/0iroN/trvision) - trvision implements direct USB control of Thermalright Vision display panels using previously documented protocol research. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/trvision-case/)</sub>

- [**xbloom-ble: a client for the xBloom Studio BLE protocol**](https://github.com/Janczykkkko/xbloom-ble) - xbloom-ble implements a Python client for the xBloom Studio coffee machine's recovered Bluetooth LE protocol. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/xbloom-ble-case/)</sub>

- [**a0rfid: an open driver for A0-protocol UHF RFID readers**](https://github.com/uaih3k9x/a0rfid) - Reconstructs the A0 serial protocol of R2000-family 915 MHz UHF RFID desktop readers, which ship with only Windows software and an Android app, from the vendor app's native command encoder rather than its misleading Java SDK. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/a0rfid-uhf-reader-protocol-case/)</sub>
- [**Cat Printer BLE: reconstructing the MXW01 thermal printer protocol**](https://github.com/MaikelChan/CatPrinterBLE) - Replaces the vendor phone app for the MXW01 “cat printer”, a small Bluetooth Low Energy thermal printer, with a Windows command-line client. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/catprinterble-mxw01-printer-case/)</sub>
- [**DJI MIMO BLE artifacts: reconstructing the DJI Osmo control protocol**](https://github.com/xaionaro/reverse-engineering-dji) - Documents the Bluetooth Low Energy message format that DJI's proprietary MIMO app uses to control DJI Osmo devices, as artifacts produced while building the independent djictl CLI. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/dji-mimo-ble-reveng-case/)</sub>
- [**Ford Fiesta MK5 MS-CAN: decoding the dashboard and radio bus**](https://github.com/roncapat/Ford-Fiesta-MK5-MS-CAN-bus) - Documents the medium-speed CAN bus that links the 6000CD radio and the dashboard of a restyled (post-2006) Ford Fiesta MK5, worked out by tapping the bus at the radio's QuadLock connector with a Seeed CAN-BUS Shield on an Arduino Uno. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/ford-fiesta-mk5-ms-can-case/)</sub>
- [**opendash: reconstructing the Scanmatik SM3 J2534 adapter protocol**](https://github.com/PabloSoage/opendash) - Speaks the undocumented protocol of the Scanmatik SM3, a J2534 vehicle interface that otherwise talks only to its own Windows software, and exposes it to an Android phone as an ELM327 bridge with a diagnostics app on top. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/opendash-scanmatik-sm3-protocol-case/)</sub>
- [**OWL: an open Apple Wireless Direct Link implementation**](https://github.com/seemoo-lab/owl) - Reimplements Apple Wireless Direct Link (AWDL), the proprietary Wi-Fi ad hoc protocol Apple devices use for peer-to-peer links such as AirDrop, as a user-space C daemon for Linux and macOS; the README calls it the result of reverse engineering by the Open Wireless Link project at TU Darmstadt's SEEMOO lab. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/owl-awdl-open-implementation-case/)</sub>
- [**uniden-r8-ble: reconstructing the Uniden R8 radar detector's BLE telemetry**](https://github.com/JeremyWhittaker/unidenr8_bluetooth) - Decodes the undocumented Bluetooth Low Energy output of a Uniden R8 radar detector into a receive-only collector for a Raspberry Pi, with live telemetry, alert start/update/end events, SQLite history and optional MQTT and Home Assistant publishing. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/uniden-r8-ble-telemetry-case/)</sub>
- [**Xiaomi Kettle BLE protocol: reconstructing a smart kettle's control interface**](https://github.com/anna-oake/xiaomi-kettle) - Documents the closed Bluetooth Low Energy GATT protocol of the Xiaomi Kettle, which the author reconstructed by decompiling the Mi Home Android app and disassembling its native encryption library. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/xiaomi-kettle-ble-protocol-case/)</sub>
- [**bosectl: reconstructing Bose’s BMAP headphone protocol**](https://github.com/aaronsb/bosectl) - Controls Bose headphones from Linux and macOS without the Bose app, account or cloud, through Python, Rust and C++ libraries and command-line tools that implement Bose’s BMAP protocol over Bluetooth RFCOMM. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/bosectl-bose-bmap-protocol-case/)</sub>
- [**BudsPro-Headtracking: streaming Galaxy Buds Pro head tracking over Samsung’s serial protocol**](https://github.com/timschneeb/BudsPro-Headtracking) - Reimplements the Samsung Galaxy Buds Pro’s proprietary spatial-audio messages in a small Python script so that a PC can stream the earbuds’ head-tracking data in real time. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/budspro-headtracking-case/)</sub>
- [**Even G2 protocol: reverse-engineering Even Realities G2 smart-glasses BLE traffic**](https://github.com/i-soxi/even-g2-protocol) - Documents the Bluetooth Low Energy protocol between the Even app and Even Realities G2 smart glasses, worked out from captured traffic: GATT characteristic UUIDs, an 8-byte transport header with sequence, multi-packet and two-byte service-ID fields, a CRC-16/CCITT over the payload, and protobuf payloads with draft .proto definitions. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/even-g2-ble-protocol-case/)</sub>
- [**fuji-cam-wifi-tool: reconstructing Fujifilm X-series Wi-Fi remote control**](https://github.com/hkr/fuji-cam-wifi-tool) - Reimplements the Wi-Fi remote-control protocol of Fujifilm X-series cameras as a C++ library and an interactive command-line client that joins the camera's access point. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/fuji-cam-wifi-tool-protocol-case/)</sub>
- [**garmin-ble: a Python client for Garmin's GFDI watch protocol**](https://github.com/gwerneckp/garmin-ble) - Python library that talks to Garmin watches over their proprietary GFDI V2 Bluetooth LE protocol, with no Garmin Connect, phone or cloud service. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/garmin-ble-gfdi-protocol-case/)</sub>
- [**Gymnasticon: bridging proprietary exercise-bike data to standard cycling sensors**](https://github.com/ptx2/gymnasticon) - Node.js bridge that reads power and cadence from exercise bikes whose own apps or services are gone or closed, and re-broadcasts them as standard Bluetooth LE Cycling Power and Cycling Speed and Cadence sensors and as an ANT+ bike power profile, so that Zwift, TrainerRoad, bike computers and watches can use the bike. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/gymnasticon-exercise-bike-bridge-case/)</sub>
